artifact.summary: Single-qubit circuit for an alternating two-axis SU(2) rotation sequence U = R_{jN}(theta_N)...R_{j1}(theta_1). Axis 1 is z. Axis 2 lies in the x-z plane at angle alpha from z, so n2 = (sin alpha, 0, cos alpha). R_1 is rz(theta). R_2 is ry(-alpha), rz(theta), ry(alpha) in time order. Segment 1 acts first. The time cost, the time-optimal search and the angle bounds are not part of the circuit.
register_layout: qubit 0: the single data qubit on which the SU(2) sequence acts; Qiskit little-endian, only one qubit
Axis 1 = Bloch z axis; axis 2 = (sin alpha, 0, cos alpha), in the x-z plane
Segments are applied in list order (segment 1 first)

equation_mapping.code_location: build_circuit: axis==1 branch (qc.rz) and axis==2 branch (ry(-alpha), rz, ry(alpha))
equation_mapping.explanation: R_j(theta)=exp(-i theta n_j.sigma/2). n1=z and n2=(sin alpha,0,cos alpha) give n1.n2=cos alpha. R_2 is built by conjugating Rz with Ry(alpha).

equation_mapping.code_location: build_circuit: loop over segments with the alternating-axis check
equation_mapping.explanation: Gates are appended in time order, so the operator is R_{jN}...R_{j1}. Consecutive segments on the same axis raise ValueError.
The time cost depends on the speeds Omega_j, which a unitary circuit does not use. The circuit takes angles directly. The only trace of the cost model is the clockwise-only check theta>=0.
The time-optimal synthesis is a classical numerical optimization, not a circuit.
N<=5 is a property of optimal sequences, not a constraint on arbitrary sequences. The builder does not enforce it. Segments are only limited to 50.

specification_changes.change: Fixed the axes to n1=z and n2=(sin alpha,0,cos alpha) in the x-z plane.
specification_changes.reason: The abstract does not fix the axes. Only the angle between them matters, up to a global frame rotation.

specification_changes.change: Narrowed scope to applying a given sequence. There is no speed ratio, time cost, optimization, or enforced N<=5 bound.
specification_changes.reason: The abstract gives no explicit angle bounds, parametrization, or search procedure, and a circuit implements the operation, not the optimization.

specification_changes.change: Segment lists must alternate axes, and angles are real. With allow_counterclockwise=false, angles must be nonnegative, with no reduction mod 2pi.
specification_changes.reason: This is a simple validation of the clockwise-only variant.

assumptions: Each rotation is exp(-i theta n.sigma/2) with Pauli sigma, applied to one qubit.
Segments are given in time order.
The global phase is zero, because the standard rz, ry gates are used.
No target unitary is supplied. The caller provides the angles.
unresolved_issues: The explicit angle bounds and the three-angle parametrization of optimal sequences are not in the abstract.
The clockwise-only scaling laws are not implemented.
No time-optimal angles are computed. The example angles are arbitrary.

validation.detail: Circuit built and transpiled successfully; no independent correctness reference selected.
